name: Dedan
title: Descendants of Cush and Abraham
summary: Dedan is a name that appears several times in the Bible, both as a grandson of Cush through Raamah (Gen 10:7) and as a grandson of Abraham through Keturah and her son Jokshan (Gen 25:3). Dedan became the ancestor of an Arab people and trading nation who lived in the northwestern part of the Arabian Peninsula. The prophets Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel mention Dedan in connection with trade and prophecies about judgment.

keyEvents.title: Dedan as a descendant of Cush
keyEvents.description: In the genealogy of Noah's descendants, Dedan is mentioned as a son of Rama, who was a son of Cush. This links Dedan to the Hamitic peoples.

keyEvents.title: Dedan as a descendant of Abraham
keyEvents.description: Dedan is also mentioned as a son of Jokshan, who was a son of Abraham and his other wife Keturah. His sons were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's prophecy about Dedan
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah mentions Dedan in a prophecy concerning Arabia, where caravans from Dedan must seek refuge in the forest due to coming destruction.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah prophesies judgment over Dedan
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah includes Dedan among the nations that will drink from the cup of the Lord's wrath and warns the people of Dedan to flee.

keyEvents.title: Ezekiel mentions Dedan's trade activities
keyEvents.description: In Ezekiel's lament over Tyre, Dedan is described as a significant trading partner who dealt in saddle blankets and other goods.

keyEvents.title: Ezekiel's prophecy about Gog and Dedan
keyEvents.description: In the prophecy concerning Gog from the land of Magog, Sheba and Dedan are mentioned among those who question Gog's invasion of Israel.
